Resolve the entity before the story
A brand is not a legal person, and a group chart is not proof of control.

Map parent companies, insurers, policy brands, administrators, providers, investors, lenders, suppliers and subcontractors. Label every relationship by type and date: ownership, contract, financing, shared service, governance, brand or unresolved.
Choose one insurer. Build a map with at least five distinct entity types. Add a source and date to every arrow; mark unsupported links as hypotheses.
Turn the public claim into testable claims
Marketing language often compresses several different promises into one sentence.
Capture exact wording, speaker, date, audience, scope and measurable proposition. Split claims about access, quality, speed, choice, outcomes and accountability.
Rewrite “care within reach for everyone” into four separate claims and specify what evidence could test each.
Build a source register and provenance trail
A source is a record with an origin, purpose, date, scope and limitation.

Record source ID, publisher, author, date, version, source type, URL/path, page, original/copy status and known dependencies. Distinguish primary records, summaries, promotional material and anonymous tips.
Find a registry filing, annual report, contract extract and customer-facing page. Explain the different questions each can answer.
Assess evidence and confidence separately
A narrow fact can be well established while the wider theory remains unknown.

Use Supported / Partly supported / Disputed / Unknown / Outdated for evidence status; High / Medium / Low / Unknown for confidence. Explain scope and why confidence is not a score for how plausible a story feels.
Assess one claim twice: status and confidence. Then write what additional source would change either assessment.
Trace money, incentives and motives
Follow incentives without assuming that an incentive proves conduct.

Map shareholdings, debt, dividends, asset sales, procurement, related-party contracts, land, energy exposure, family ownership and executive compensation. Separate documented financial interests from inferred motives.
For one company, identify a plausible commercial incentive, the source that establishes it, and at least two alternative explanations for the same decision.
Follow the supplier and platform layer
Shared software can create dependencies without creating a single controlling organisation.

Trace platform contracts, service schedules, data-processing roles, subcontractors, procurement decisions, migration tickets, service-level metrics and exit clauses. A logo or login screen does not prove data access or control.
Investigate the ubiquitous workflow vendor. Find what it can establish, what it merely points toward, and which contract annexes remain missing.
Triangulate, do not stack citations
Several documents repeating one press release are still one information lineage.
Trace source lineage, identify copied figures, compare independent records, test chronology and preserve contradictions. Record who benefits from publication and what the source could not know.
Find two apparently corroborating sources. Determine whether they are independent, derived from a common dataset or simply repeating the same statement.
Test practical access and lived outcomes
A directory entry, contract or visible slot is not an appointment or a successful outcome.

For care access, seek named provider, site, treatment, service code, referral, contract period, capacity, wait-time and member-level outcome evidence. Distinguish entitlement, contractual coverage and practical availability.
Choose one care pathway. List the evidence needed to follow a person from referral through treatment and payment. Mark each missing link.
Interrogate metrics and compare like with like
A percentage without a unit, denominator, period and exclusions is a headline, not a finding.

Distinguish people, interactions, tickets, locations, organisations, addresses, slots, claims and episodes. Check deduplication, missing data, eligibility, time windows, category changes and revisions.
Compare two company metrics and one vendor dashboard. Explain why their percentages cannot safely be ranked.
Build competing explanations and a bounded conclusion
The strongest investigation is not the one with the biggest reveal. It is the one that survives alternatives.

Maintain a hypothesis ledger: explanation, supporting evidence, contradictory evidence, missing evidence, confidence and falsifier. Consider ordinary administration, commercial incentives, fragmented systems, error, misconduct and mixed explanations. State what would change your mind.
Write a finding, a competing explanation, an unresolved question and a precise document request. Do not force a single hidden-controller theory from circumstantial links.
